past_medical_history: No prior medical or psychiatric history

patient.chief_complaint: New-onset seizures, personality change, orofacial dyskinesias, and autonomic instability over 2 weeks
patient.history_present_illness: A 24-year-old right-handed woman with no prior medical or psychiatric history was brought to the emergency department by ambulance after her roommate witnessed a generalized tonic-clonic seizure lasting approximately 90 seconds. Family and roommates describe a 2-week history of progressive behavioral change that began with insomnia, then progressed to paranoid ideation, visual hallucinations, and agitation. Approximately one week into this presentation she began making repetitive grimacing facial movements and repetitive chewing motions that were not under her control. During the week prior to admission she also had two shorter staring spells with lip-smacking that her roommates recognized as seizure-like activity. She was seen at urgent care four days ago and sent home with a tentative diagnosis of substance-induced psychosis, but her urine drug screen was negative. Her parents note that she had a febrile illness with headache, sore throat, and malaise approximately 3 weeks before the behavioral change began, lasting about 5-6 days, that resolved on its own. On the day of admission, she had the witnessed GTCS followed by a prolonged post-ictal state. On arrival she is intermittently agitated and has obvious orofacial dyskinesias. Her blood pressure has ranged from 96/58 to 168/94 in the past hour.

neurological_exam.mental_status: Intermittently agitated and confused. Not oriented to time or place. Unable to cooperate with formal cognitive testing. Continuous orofacial dyskinesias with lip-smacking, tongue-thrusting, and grimacing observed. Intermittent echolalia.
neurological_exam.cranial_nerves: Pupils equal, 4mm, reactive. EOMs intact. Continuous involuntary orofacial movements involving lips, tongue, jaw, and periorbital muscles.
neurological_exam.motor: Mild choreoathetosis of bilateral upper extremities. Full strength on brief cooperative exam. Tone mildly increased.
neurological_exam.additional: Autonomic instability: BP 148/92 currently, HR 122, diaphoresis, temperature 38.0. No nuchal rigidity.

findings.frequency: Delta 1-1.5 Hz with superimposed 30-40 Hz beta bursts
findings.morphology: Classic extreme delta brush (EDB) pattern — pathognomonic for anti-NMDAR encephalitis. Delta waves with superimposed high-frequency beta activity giving a 'brushing' appearance.
Generalized rhythmic delta activity between EDB bursts
Two electrographic seizures captured during recording; both began focally in right temporal region and generalized

eeg.impression: Two electrographic seizures captured. Generalized encephalopathy with continuous EDB. Clinical correlation recommended.

signal_characteristics.description: Bilateral FLAIR/T2 hyperintensity in hippocampi and amygdalae

mri.impression: Subtle cortical FLAIR changes also noted. No enhancement. No diffusion restriction. Clinical correlation recommended.

output.proposed: Levetiracetam 1500 mg BID + methylprednisolone 1g IV daily + IVIG 0.4 g/kg/day
interactions: Corticosteroids and IVIG: minimal interactions with levetiracetam
warnings: IVIG requires adequate hydration to prevent thromboembolic events
alternatives: Lacosamide as alternative antiseizure agent if levetiracetam insufficient

differential.key_features: Temporal FLAIR signal — but bilateral, HSV PCR negative, EDB pattern on EEG is pathognomonic for anti-NMDAR
Seizures present — but EDB pattern and clinical triad point to specific diagnosis
Viral prodrome, pleocytosis — but all viral PCRs negative, EDB pathognomonic

optimal_actions.action: LP with anti-NMDAR antibodies, HSV PCR, full panel
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Lymphocytic pleocytosis; anti-NMDAR positive; HSV negative

critical_actions: EEG showing extreme delta brush is essentially pathognomonic — initiate immunotherapy without waiting for antibody confirmation
Anti-NMDAR antibody testing (serum and CSF) is confirmatory
Pelvic imaging is mandatory — right ovarian teratoma identified
Antiseizure therapy required — electrographic seizures documented
SIADH with Na 128 requires fluid restriction and careful management
contraindicated_actions: Discharging with substance-induced psychosis diagnosis — drug screen was negative
Delaying immunotherapy waiting for antibody confirmation when EDB on EEG is present
Rapid saline correction of hyponatremia — risk of osmotic demyelination
key_reasoning_points: Classic anti-NMDAR encephalitis triad: psychiatric prodrome → seizures → orofacial dyskinesias → autonomic instability, in a young woman
Extreme delta brush on EEG is essentially pathognomonic for anti-NMDAR encephalitis
Bilateral medial temporal FLAIR hyperintensity is consistent with (though not universal in) anti-NMDAR encephalitis
Viral prodrome 3 weeks prior is the typical antecedent trigger
Very high antibody titers (serum 1:320) correlate with severity of clinical presentation
Teratoma found in right ovary — resection is the most important treatment step alongside immunotherapy

metadata.difficulty_variant_description: Classic straightforward anti-NMDAR encephalitis: 24-year-old with full triad (psychiatric prodrome, seizures, orofacial dyskinesias, autonomic instability), bilateral temporal MRI changes, extreme delta brush on EEG, positive CSF antibodies.
